rows.label: Display Mode
rows.help: Windowed, fullscreen, or a borderless window that fills the screen.

rows.label: Resolution
rows.help: Size of the window or the fullscreen picture. A: full list. Left/Right: next size.

rows.label: Aspect Ratio
rows.help: Auto fills the window. The others keep that shape and add black bars.

rows.label: 3D Resolution
rows.help: Detail of the 3D world. Original renders at the GameCube's 480 lines, the lightest and the default. Higher looks sharper, lower runs faster.

rows.label: Refresh Rate
rows.help: How often the screen updates in fullscreen. Auto keeps your monitor's setting.

rows.label: Frame Sync (VSync)
rows.help: Waits for the screen before showing each frame. Stops tearing (a picture split in two), adds a little input delay.

rows.label: FPS Mode
rows.help: Frames per second. 30 is the original and the most stable. 60 and 120 are smoother but experimental.

rows.label: Antialiasing
rows.help: Smooths jagged edges on characters and scenery. Small performance cost.

rows.label: Texture Filtering
rows.help: Keeps the ground and walls sharp when seen at an angle. Higher costs a little performance.

rows.label: Lighting
rows.help: Smooth: softer, more detailed light on characters. Original: as on GameCube.

rows.label: Shadows
rows.help: Original draws the game's own soft shadows under characters and objects. Soft, Normal and Strong replace them with real-time shadows from the sun.

rows.label: Fog
rows.help: The game's own distance fog. On is how the original looks.

rows.label: Bloom
rows.help: Soft glow around bright lights and bright areas.

rows.label: Ambient Occlusion
rows.help: Soft shadows in corners and where objects meet the ground.

rows.label: Depth of Field
rows.help: Blurs the far distance so what is close to you stands out.

rows.label: Colour Adjustments
rows.help: Turns on the Gamma, Brightness and Saturation sliders below. Off shows the original colours.

rows.label: Texture Packs
rows.help: Replacement textures made by the community. Install one from its zip or switch between them. Changes need a restart.

rows.label: HD Models
rows.help: High-detail character models. Install each one from its zip, then turn it On or Off.

rows.label: Red Pikmin
rows.help: Model for the red Pikmin: the game's, or one made with the Model Maker (Load/Pikmin). The leaf, bud and flower stay the game's.

rows.label: Yellow Pikmin
rows.help: Model for the yellow Pikmin: the game's, or one made with the Model Maker (Load/Pikmin). The leaf, bud and flower stay the game's.

rows.label: Blue Pikmin
rows.help: Model for the blue Pikmin: the game's, or one made with the Model Maker (Load/Pikmin). The leaf, bud and flower stay the game's.

rows.label: Controller Layout
rows.help: What each controller button does. GameCube: the original layout. Switch: as in Pikmin 1 + 2 on Switch (right stick turns the camera, L + right stick swarms, ZL faces forward, ZR zooms). Buttons you reassigned keep your choice.

rows.label: Right Stick Aim
rows.help: Connect a controller first.

rows.label: Controller Guide
rows.help: Every controller button and what it does right now, sorted by topic. It follows the layout, your reassigned buttons and the mods you have on.

rows.label: Keyboard Bindings
rows.help: Two keys or mouse buttons per action. A: main key. Right: second key. Left: back to default. While waiting, Delete clears it. Shift, Ctrl and Alt can be used.

rows.label: Controller Bindings
rows.help: Choose the controller button for each action.

rows.label: Control Scheme
rows.help: Classic: the stick moves the cursor, as on GameCube. Mouse Cursor: aim the cursor with the mouse.

rows.label: Mouse Wheel
rows.help: What the mouse wheel does: choose the Pikmin colour to throw, or zoom the camera.

rows.label: Hold to Pluck
rows.help: Hold the pluck button to pull up sprouts one after another.

rows.label: Whistle Pluck
rows.help: Hold the whistle over sprouts to pluck them one after another.

rows.label: Throw While Moving
rows.help: Throw Pikmin while running, instead of Olimar stopping first.

rows.label: Cancel a Throw
rows.help: While holding a Pikmin ready to throw, press B (the cancel button) to put it back in the squad.

rows.label: Quick Grab
rows.help: The next Pikmin jumps straight into Olimar's hand, so throwing stays fast even with the squad behind him.

rows.label: Pikmin 2 Selection
rows.help: D-pad as in Pikmin 2. Left/Right chooses the colour for every throw. Hold A and press Up/Down to pick leaf, bud, flower or a Yellow with a bomb rock. Off: Left/Right only picks the next throw.

rows.label: Onion: Move 10 at a Time
rows.help: In the Onion menu, hold Y while pressing up or down to move 10 Pikmin at a time.

rows.label: Bomb Control
rows.help: Bomb button (B on keyboard, set a controller button in Controls): a Yellow with a bomb rock throws it at the cursor, or drops it at its feet if the cursor is too close. Yellows already thrown go first.

rows.label: Bomb Rock Respawn
rows.help: Used bomb rock piles grow back one rock at a time during the same day, instead of only the next morning.

rows.label: Lock-On
rows.help: Automatic: locks onto the nearest enemy or object as you approach. Manual: press the Lock-On button (set it in Controls).

rows.label: Stick Dead Zone
rows.help: Ignores tiny stick movements. Raise it if the cursor or Olimar moves on its own (stick drift).

rows.label: Stick Invert
rows.help: Flips the movement stick: horizontal, vertical or both.

rows.label: Camera Stick Invert
rows.help: Flips the right stick (the GameCube C-Stick): horizontal, vertical or both.

rows.label: Gyro Aiming
rows.help: Aim the cursor by tilting a controller with motion sensors, or your phone. In first person it looks around.

rows.label: Free Camera
rows.help: Turn the camera freely, as in Pikmin 3. Mouse: push the cursor against the edge of its circle. Controller: right stick. L puts the camera back behind Olimar. Swarming moves to the Swarm button (assign it in Controls).

rows.label: Free Camera Speed
rows.help: How fast the right stick turns the free camera. 100% is the default.

rows.label: First Person
rows.help: Look at the world from inside Olimar's helmet. Switch in game with the First Person button (V on keyboard, L3 on a controller).

rows.label: Co-op Split Screen
rows.help: How the screen divides in two-player co-op.

rows.label: Co-op Merged Camera
rows.help: Joins both halves into one view while the captains are close.

rows.label: Instant Whistle Response
rows.help: Whistled Pikmin join the squad at once, without stopping to turn and look first.

rows.label: Chain Pikmin Actions
rows.help: Pikmin that finish a task go on to the next one nearby.

rows.label: Better Pathfinding
rows.help: Smarter Pikmin: they get unstuck on their way, and no longer stop to pull nectar grass they walk past (swarm them at it instead).

rows.label: Thrown Pikmin Return
rows.help: A thrown Pikmin that lands with nothing to do runs back to the squad. Leave this off to finish the game: some areas need a Pikmin left on a ledge or across water while you move Olimar.

rows.label: Blues Only In Water
rows.help: Only blue Pikmin walk into water on their own.

rows.label: No Tripping
rows.help: Pikmin running in the squad never trip and fall behind.

rows.label: Eternal Night
rows.help: Always night, whatever the day length: night lighting, and the moon crosses the day bar instead of the sun.

rows.label: Fireflies
rows.help: Fireflies drift around the field, by day or by night.

rows.label: Idle Pikmin Counter
rows.help: Shows how many Pikmin are standing around with nothing to do.

rows.label: Hide Olimar's Messages
rows.help: Skips the messages Olimar shows while you play (first Pikmin, ship parts, tips). The ending messages still appear.

rows.label: Day Length
rows.help: Minutes of daylight per day. 13.5 is the original; Infinite stops the sun, except on the last day.

rows.label: Olimar Health
rows.help: Olimar's toughness, as a share of the original. Infinite takes no damage.

rows.label: Enemy Health
rows.help: Enemy toughness, as a share of the original. Insta Kill drops them in one hit.

rows.label: Pikmin Limit
rows.help: Most Pikmin on the field at once. 100 is the original; more costs performance.

rows.label: Throw Speed
rows.help: How fast Olimar grabs and throws Pikmin. 100% is the original.

rows.label: Whistle Radius
rows.help: Size of the whistle circle at full charge. 100% is the original.

rows.label: Invincible Pikmin
rows.help: Pikmin never die: no attacks, fire, water, gas or crushing.

rows.label: All Flowers
rows.help: Every Pikmin grows a flower as soon as it is plucked or born.

rows.label: Carry Speed
rows.help: How fast Pikmin carry pellets, parts and bodies.

rows.label: Olimar Speed
rows.help: How fast Olimar walks and runs.

rows.label: Unlock All Zones
rows.help: Opens every area on the map. Saved into your game.

rows.label: No Day Limit
rows.help: The day counter never advances, so the 30-day limit never comes.

rows.label: All Onions
rows.help: Red, Yellow and Blue Onions from the start. Saved into your game.

rows.label: Breakable Reinforced Gates
rows.help: Pikmin can break the black reinforced gates by hitting them, without bomb rocks.

rows.label: Debug Keys (F5-F8)
rows.help:
F5: add up to 20 red leaf Pikmin to the red Onion (requires an Onion and respects the Pikmin limit).
F6: advance the clock by one in-game hour, capped just before sunset (with Infinite Day it only moves the lighting, except on the last day).
F7: grant the Main Engine, top red Onion stock up to 20, and trigger the normal end-of-day sequence.
F8 (VS only): append both captains' XYZ coordinates to vs_positions.txt.
With Quick Save on, F6 is Quick Save and F7 is Quick Load.
